item.title: Scholarship as Struggle: Stories of Censorship, Marketisation, and Resistance
item.content:encoded:
Rebecca Elliott, London School of Economics and Political Science

Sam Friedman, London School of Economics and Political Science

Ali Meghji, University of Cambridge

Aaron Reeves, University of Oxford

This project invites sociologists and scholars from around the world to reflect on the challenges facing higher education, including political censorship, marketisation, and institutional attacks on academic freedom. The call recognises that these pressures manifest differently across countries, from overt censorship in some nations to decades of marketisation and budget cuts in others, resulting in department closures and job losses.

The journal seeks commentary pieces that examine these conditions through multiple lenses: personal experiences situated within structural realities, historical and political analysis of current crises, and explorations of potential solutions. The project aims to provide a sustained platform for marginalised voices and to address long-term challenges facing academia globally, rather than serving as a short-term response to individual crises.

Appel publié par British Journal of Sociology. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Personal experiences of censorship and marketisation in higher education in light of structural conditions
  • Historical, political, economic, and cultural underpinnings of current crises in academia
  • Potential solutions and transformations to address attacks on higher education
  • Global perspectives on the conditions facing sociologists and scholars across different countries
  • Impact of political censorship, xenophobia, and budget cuts on academic freedom and employment

Timeline

  • September 30, 2026: Submission deadline

item.title: The New Sociology of Propaganda
item.content:encoded:
Freeden Blume Oeur, Tufts University

Fiona Greenland, University of Virginia

This special issue addresses propaganda as a contemporary social problem requiring updated sociological research. While propaganda shaped public opinion during the imperial era through the Cold War, modern contexts present new challenges: AI-generated content blurs reality, traditional and digital media proliferate messaging, and state and non-state actors compete to control information. The issue seeks research examining how propaganda operates today, the technologies and techniques it employs, and the power structures it reinforces or challenges.

The special issue welcomes empirical, historical, and theoretical contributions from all sociological subfields and methodologies examining propaganda globally. Research should explore the actors behind propaganda, those targeted by it, resistance efforts, and how propaganda intersects with broader social phenomena like authoritarianism, censorship, and polarization. The aim is to establish social scientific research directions on propaganda for the coming decades.

Appel publié par British Journal of Sociology. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • How modern propaganda operates and its social consequences
  • How propaganda campaigns reveal power dynamics and their relationship to systems of oppression and violence
  • The machinery of modern propaganda: symbols, slogans, advertisements, techniques, and technologies (traditional and emerging)
  • Actors creating propaganda and their targets
  • Propaganda's role in major conflicts and crises including wars and climate change
  • Resistance and counteraction to propaganda
  • How people understand and use propaganda in everyday life
  • Connections between propaganda and related sociological topics such as censorship, schooling, radicalization, authoritarianism, polarization, religion, power and persuasion, memory and commemoration, misinformation and disinformation
  • Spread of propaganda campaigns within and across communities and borders
  • Methods for detecting and avoiding propaganda's potential harms

Timeline

  • October 30, 2026: Full Manuscript Submission Deadline
